usage: This is the standard, everyday way to ask if someone speaks English across the Levant. Because of the verb root, 'bti7ki' is written and pronounced the same for both masculine and feminine singular, though some speakers might slightly elongate the final vowel for females. It is perfectly acceptable for strangers, but you can add 'law sama7t' (excuse me) to be more polite.

variants.label: to a man or woman
variants.note: The standard form, identical for addressing a single man or woman.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: indirect/polite (to a man)
variants.english: Do you know how to speak English?
variants.note: A slightly softer, less direct way to ask a man.

variants.label: indirect/polite (to a woman)
variants.english: Do you know how to speak English?
variants.note: A slightly softer, less direct way to ask a woman.

examples.english: Excuse me, do you speak English?

examples.arabic: أنا ما بحكي عربي منيح، بتحكي إنجليزي؟
examples.transliteration: ana ma ba7ki 3arabi mnee7, bti7ki injleezi?
examples.english: I don't speak Arabic well, do you speak English?
Do you guys speak English or should I translate?
